chunks: (And) said: "These two are surely magicians. They want to deprive you of your land with their magic, and eradicate your distinct way (of life)."
ai.seo_question: What did the Israelites say about Musa and Harun regarding their magic and plan to leave Egypt?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Taa-Haa, this verse captures the psychological resistance of the Israelites, who, despite witnessing divine signs, preferred the familiar stability of Pharaoh’s rule over the transformative challenge of prophethood. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a critique of clinging to ancestral traditions ('tarīqat al-muthlā') even when they are rooted in falsehood, illustrating the human tendency to view radical spiritual truth as disruptive sorcery.
